title_en: Jin Gong Company v. Guangfa Company — dispute over jurisdiction objection concerning commercial housing sales contract
ruling_gist_en: In accordance with the provisions of Article 18 of the Arbitration Law, if the arbitration agreement does not specify or specifies unclearly the matters to be arbitrated or the arbitration commission, the parties may enter into a supplementary agreement; if they fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement shall be invalid. In accordance with the provisions of Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on Several Issues Concerning Confirmation of the Validity of Arbitration Agreements, if, after the implementation of the Arbitration Law but before the reestablishment of arbitration institutions, the parties concluded an arbitration agreement that only specifies the place of arbitration but fails to specify the arbitration institution, and the parties select in a supplementary agreement an arbitration institution that has been lawfully reestablished at that place, the arbitration agreement is valid; if the parties fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement is invalid. Where the arbitration agreement is determined to be invalid in accordance with the above provisions, and a party files a lawsuit with a competent people's court, the people's court shall accept the case.

full_text_en:
Jinggong Company v. Guangfa Company — dispute over jurisdiction in a commercial housing sale contract

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 18 of the Arbitration Law of the PRC, if an arbitration agreement fails to specify or clearly specify the arbitration matters or the arbitration commission, the parties may reach a supplementary agreement; if they fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement is invalid. According to Article 1 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Confirmation of the Validity of Arbitration Agreements, if, after the implementation of the Arbitration Law but before the restructuring of arbitration institutions, the parties enter into an arbitration agreement that only specifies the place of arbitration but does not specify the arbitration institution, and the parties, in a supplementary agreement, select an arbitration institution lawfully restructured at that place, the arbitration agreement is valid; if the parties fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement is invalid. Where an arbitration agreement is found invalid in accordance with the above provisions, and a party files a lawsuit with a competent people's court, the people's court shall accept the case.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 11

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Jingdezhen Jinggong Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at 4th Floor, Xinyue Building, Zhushan Middle Road, Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Xinyue, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yaoquan, lawyer of Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Jingdezhen Guangfa Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at 4th Floor, Building B, No. 473 Zhonghua South Road, Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Xiang Genji, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Lanying, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lan Weidong, lawyer of Jiangxi Qiuzheng Wode Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a commercial housing sale contract between the appellant Jingdezhen Jinggong Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinggong Company) and the appellee Jingdezhen Guangfa Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangfa Company), the Jiangxi High People's Court rendered a civil ruling on December 9, 2005, dismissing the jurisdictional objection raised by Jinggong Company. Jinggong Company, dissatisfied with the ruling, appealed to this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and conducted an inquiry with both parties on February 20, 2006. The agent ad litem of Jinggong Company, Chen Yaoquan, and the agents ad litem of Guangfa Company, Sun Lanying and Lan Weidong, participated in the inquiry. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following after trial: Jinggong Company raised a jurisdictional objection within the defense period. On November 11, 2005, the court of first instance convened a hearing with both Jinggong Company and Guangfa Company regarding the grounds for the jurisdictional objection raised by Jinggong Company.

Jinggong Company raised the following jurisdictional objection: 1. Regarding the scope of acceptance, the dispute is not within the jurisdiction of the people's court. The parties had already reached an agreement in the Supplementary Agreements signed on March 7, 2004, and September 7, 2004, to submit to arbitration by a local arbitration institution. According to Article 5 of the Arbitration Law of the PRC, this case should not be under the jurisdiction of the people's court. Pursuant to the Letter on the Establishment of Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission (No. [1995] 135) issued by the Jiangxi Provincial People's Government on October 16, 1995, the case should be accepted by the Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission. 2. It violates the provisions on territorial jurisdiction. The applicant is a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. According to relevant judicial interpretations, the first instance of this case shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Court of the provincial capital, i.e., Nanchang. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Which Level of People's Court Shall Have Jurisdiction over Objections to the Validity of Arbitration Agreements provides that if the parties fail to specify or clearly specify the arbitration commission, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the intermediate people's court at the place where the defendant is domiciled. Even if the case is under the jurisdiction of the people's court, it should be under the jurisdiction of the Jingdezhen Intermediate People's Court. 3. There is a problem with hierarchical jurisdiction. According to information from industry insiders, the starting threshold for accepting first-instance civil cases in the Jiangxi High People's Court is RMB 50 million or more, while the subject matter of this case is only about RMB 30 million. According to the internal rules on hierarchical jurisdiction of the people's courts, the case should also be under the jurisdiction of the Jingdezhen Intermediate People's Court. Therefore, the case should either be under the jurisdiction of the Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission or under the jurisdiction of a competent intermediate people's court.

Guangfa Company replied: There are five agreements between the parties, of which only two contain arbitration clauses, and both arbitration clauses fail to clearly specify the arbitration institution. The other three agreements do not contain any arbitration clause. Therefore, the people's court still has jurisdiction over this case. Furthermore, according to the list of mainland arbitration commissions attached to the Arrangement of the Supreme People's Court on Mutual Enforcement of Arbitral Awards between Mainland and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (Fa Shi [2000] No. 3), as of May 31, 1999, only three arbitration commissions were established in Jiangxi Province in accordance with the Arbitration Law of the PRC: Nanchang, Xinyu, and Pingxiang. Thus, the legality of the so-called Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission can be excluded.

The court of first instance held: This case involves a real estate sale dispute, which is a dispute arising from immovable property. According to Article 34(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the immovable property is located. The immovable property involved in the sale in this case is located within Jiangxi Province. The acceptance of this case by the Jiangxi High People's Court does not violate the provisions on exclusive jurisdiction. The objection raised by Jinggong Company regarding territorial jurisdiction does not comply with the law. In addition, according to paragraph 4 of Article 1 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Acceptance of First-Instance Civil and Economic Dispute Cases by Higher People's Courts (Fa Fa [1999] No. 11) dated April 9, 1999, the subject matter of this case exceeds RMB 10 million, meeting the threshold for acceptance by the Jiangxi High People's Court.

Regarding the arbitration clause issue. Jinggong Company and Zheng Yuntuan signed four agreements: the House Sale Agreement dated November 26, 2003, and the Supplementary Agreements dated March 7, 2004, April 7, 2004, and September 7, 2004. Among them, the House Sale Agreement of November 26, 2003 contains no arbitration clause. Article 14 of the Supplementary Agreement of March 7, 2004 provides: "Matters not covered shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to a local arbitration institution for arbitration." The Supplementary Agreement of April 7, 2004 contains no arbitration clause. Article 6 of the Supplementary Agreement of September 7, 2004 provides: "Matters not covered shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to a local arbitration institution for arbitration." Zheng Yuntuan and Guangfa Company signed a Property Rights Transfer Agreement (the contract does not indicate the date of signing) on December 4, 2004, Article 2 of which provides that Guangfa Company shall succeed to all rights and obligations of Zheng Yuntuan under the four aforementioned agreements. All the above agreements were signed in Jingdezhen City, and both Guangfa Company and Jinggong Company are domiciled in Jingdezhen City. From the content of the above agreements, it can be seen that Zheng Yuntuan and Jinggong Company agreed to resolve disputes through arbitration, and the intention is clear and definite. Whether it is the "local arbitration institution" referred to in the Supplementary Agreement of March 7, 2004, or the "local arbitration commission" referred to in the Supplementary Agreement of September 7, 2004, both parties intended to submit to arbitration by the Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission at the place of domicile. However, according to Article 1 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Confirmation of the Validity of Arbitration Agreements, "If, after the implementation of the Arbitration Law of the PRC but before the restructuring of arbitration institutions, the parties enter into an arbitration agreement that only specifies the place of arbitration but does not specify the arbitration institution, and the parties, in a supplementary agreement, select an arbitration institution lawfully restructured at that place, the arbitration agreement is valid; if the parties fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement is invalid." Upon investigation, although the Jiangxi Provincial People's Government approved the Jingdezhen Municipal People's Government to establish a "Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission," the Jingdezhen Municipal People's Government did not restructure a "Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission" after the implementation of the Arbitration Law of the PRC. This can be evidenced by the list of mainland arbitration commissions attached to the Arrangement of the Supreme People's Court on Mutual Enforcement of Arbitral Awards between Mainland and Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (Fa Shi [2000] No. 3). To date, Jingdezhen has not yet established an arbitration commission capable of accepting arbitration matters concerning civil and commercial disputes. If this case were to be transferred to the so-called "Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission" claimed by Jinggong Company, the dispute would fall into a situation where no institution would accept it. Guangfa Company did not choose to reach a supplementary agreement with Jinggong Company to select an arbitration institution in another location but directly filed a lawsuit with the people's court, and its legitimate right to sue should be protected. The arbitration clauses in the two Supplementary Agreements should be held invalid, and this case should be under the jurisdiction of the people's court. In summary, the application of Jinggong Company lacks legal and contractual basis. Pursuant to Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled to dismiss the jurisdictional objection raised by Jinggong Company.

Jinggong Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to this Court, requesting that the first-instance ruling be set aside and the lawsuit of Guangfa Company be dismissed. Facts and grounds: 1. The arbitration clause agreed upon by the parties is valid and effective. Both parties are enterprises in Jingdezhen City, and the place of signing and performance of the agreements is Jingdezhen City. The expressions "submitted to a local arbitration institution for arbitration" and "submitted to a local arbitration commission for arbitration" in the relevant provisions do not constitute a situation where "only the place of arbitration is specified but the arbitration institution is not specified" but should be understood as "submitted to the arbitration commission of the place of domicile, i.e., Jingdezhen." 2. The Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission was formally established on January 28, 2006, and can accept arbitration cases. The principle of party autonomy should be respected, and the dispute should be submitted for arbitration.

Guangfa Company replied: The first-instance ruling dismissing the jurisdictional objection raised by Jinggong Company has clear findings of fact and correct application of law and should be upheld in accordance with the law. Facts and grounds: 1. When the parties signed the Supplementary Agreements, no arbitration institution had been established locally, and only the place of arbitration was specified without specifying the arbitration institution, rendering the relevant arbitration agreement invalid. The Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission was only lawfully established on January 28, 2006. After the dispute arose, the parties did not reach a supplementary agreement to select the newly established arbitration institution. 2. When the court of first instance accepted the case, the arbitration institution had not yet been established, and arbitration jurisdiction can be excluded in accordance with the law.

This Court found during the second-instance trial: On September 9, 2005, Guangfa Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance against Jinggong Company as the defendant, requesting: 1. rescission of the House Sale Agreement of November 26, 2003, the Supplementary Agreement of March 7, 2004, the Supplementary Agreement of April 7, 2004, and the Supplementary Agreement of September 7, 2004, signed between Guangfa Company and Jinggong Company; 2. an order that Jinggong Company refund RMB 16,363,946.6 in cash paid by Guangfa Company for the property purchase; 3. an order that Jinggong Company pay Guangfa Company liquidated damages of RMB 3.7 million; 4. an order that Jinggong Company compensate Guangfa Company for losses of RMB 15 million; 5. an order that Jinggong Company bear all litigation costs in the case. Jinggong Company raised a jurisdictional objection with the court of first instance on October 8, 2005.

During the second-instance proceedings, Jinggong Company submitted relevant documents regarding the lawful establishment of the Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission on January 28, 2006. Guangfa Company acknowledged the fact that the Jingdezhen Arbitration Commission was lawfully established on January 28, 2006.

This Court holds: From the jurisdictional objection raised by Jinggong Company in its appeal and the defense of Guangfa Company, the focus of the dispute between the parties is whether the dispute in this case falls within the jurisdiction of the people's court.

The arbitration clauses agreed upon by the parties in this case are two: first, Article 14 of the Supplementary Agreement of March 7, 2004: "Matters not covered shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to a local arbitration institution for arbitration"; second, Article 6 of the Supplementary Agreement of September 7, 2004: "Matters not covered shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, they shall be submitted to a local arbitration commission for arbitration." From the content of the above agreements, although the parties once agreed to resolve disputes through arbitration, whether it is the "local arbitration institution" referred to in the Supplementary Agreement of March 7, 2004, or the "local arbitration commission" referred to in the Supplementary Agreement of September 7, 2004, the arbitration institution was not clearly specified. The Arbitration Law of the PRC has clear legal provisions regarding the selection of an arbitration institution agreed upon by the parties. Article 18 of that Law provides: "An arbitration agreement which fails to specify or clearly specify the arbitration matters or the arbitration commission may be supplemented by the parties; if no supplementary agreement is reached, the arbitration agreement is invalid." Article 1 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Confirmation of the Validity of Arbitration Agreements provides: "If, after the implementation of the Arbitration Law of the PRC but before the restructuring of arbitration institutions, the parties enter into an arbitration agreement that only specifies the place of arbitration but does not specify the arbitration institution, and the parties, in a supplementary agreement, select an arbitration institution lawfully restructured at that place, the arbitration agreement is valid; if the parties fail to reach a supplementary agreement, the arbitration agreement is invalid." In this case, the parties disputed the selection of the arbitration institution and did not reach a new supplementary agreement, nor did they select the arbitration institution lawfully restructured at that place. Therefore, the provisions on arbitration matters in the two Supplementary Agreements are invalid. The civil dispute falls within the scope of cases accepted by the people's court. Guangfa Company filed a lawsuit with the people's court, and having the case under the jurisdiction of the people's court is not improper. The grounds of appeal raised by Jinggong Company cannot stand and are not supported in accordance with the law. In summary, pursuant to Article 108(4) and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

Appeal dismissed, and the first-instance ruling is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by Jingdezhen Jinggong Industrial Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Feng Xiaoguang

Acting Judge: Liu Yinchun

Acting Judge: Chen Chaolun

March 10, 2006

Clerk: Wei Da

【Introduction of Presiding Judge】

Feng Xiaoguang, Senior Judge: Born in 1963, Master of Laws. Appointed as judge of the Supreme People's Court in October 2000.
